title: Bring the tmx engine up to its own R4 critical-tier floor
description: Dogfooding (2026-09-26): this repo's own gate fails on its PR-tier self-audit. The critical tier (cover.py, gate.py, rigor.py, matrix.py at R4) scores 58.0% against the 0.80 floor, with about 170 survivors untriaged; the standard tier scores 27.5% against 0.60, because pycollect.py and probation.py are exercised only by the nightly slow tier. Many cover.py survivors are search heuristics that change speed rather than the answer: pin them with efficiency properties or triage them as equivalent, with reasons.

acceptanceCriteria.text: tmx gate --matrix on the PR-tier self-audit passes the R4 critical tier (>= 0.80, every survivor killed or triaged with a reason)
Nightly-tier self-audit recorded for pycollect.py and probation.py

implementationNotes:
RE-MEASUREMENT, 2026-10-20, at the leader's direction under DEC-195 (4): #13's kills, then TS-24's reach by parametrization. Both matrices are at b7097a7 (origin/test/TS-11-tmx-critical-floor after merging origin/dev; TS-25's deterministic generation was NOT an ancestor of af8ad05, so the old head could not carry the build DEC-195 (4) requires). Critical tier only: cover.py, gate.py, rigor.py, matrix.py. Per-line 1, all mutants, seed 20261014, full suite, 8 jobs. Mutant-set digest 222210827aa01053cd8fc32c56202671a4b1467dfb8f64cd844f5eb0aecd6bae in both runs, and the mutant key sets are identical, so the two differ only in which tests ran. Artifacts: .tmx/ts13-crit-with-b7097a7.json and .tmx/ts13-crit-without-b7097a7.json (gitignored, as every .tmx artifact is).

MEASUREMENT 1: #13's kills.
- WITH #13: 106 tests, 461 mutants, 287 killed, 119 survived, 55 unreached.
- WITHOUT #13 (its two files ignored, nothing else changed): 92 tests, 461 mutants, 274 killed, 115 survived, 72 unreached.
- DELTA: +13 kills for 14 added cases = 0.929 kills per added test. That is BELOW 1, so by DEC-195 (4) it comes back to opum-doc instead of landing, and it has.
- The tool scores (62.3% with, 59.4% without) are NOT comparable to DEC-195's 0.727, for two reasons: that matrix recorded reached-equivalent mutants as their own status and this build records none, and the mutant count moved 418 -> 461 because gate.py grew under TS-26 and TS-27. The comparable quantity is the delta, not the ratio.
- Correction recorded so nobody repeats my first attempt: counting mutants whose killed-by list names only added tests gives 25, not 13. Those lists are not exhaustive for a mutant; 12 of the 25 are still killed without #13 by tests the with-run did not list. The with/without delta is the number of record.

MEASUREMENT 2: TS-24's reach by parametrization, same basis and the same digest.
- Unreached WITHOUT #13: 72 = 41 in functions that existing tests already exercise (the parametrisation candidates DEC-195 (2) asks for) + 16 import-time lines no test can reach under this coverage model (13 rigor.PROFILES constants, 2 cover.py default-argument lines, 1 gate.py module constant) + 15 in functions no test reaches.
- Unreached WITH #13: 55 = 38 parametrisation candidates + the same 16 import-time lines + 1 in a function no test reaches (gate.py load_policy:46, the Python <3.11 fallback, environment-gated rather than unreachable).
- So the 14 cases move 17 mutants from unreached to reached, and the untouched-function bucket from 15 to 1.
- Of #13's 13 kills: 6 were already reached but SURVIVED without it, so the cases distinguish what existing tests only touched; 7 were unreached, and of those three (cover.py certificate and check_certificate) sit in functions existing tests already exercise, while four (gate.py main x3, write_baseline x1) are reached by nothing else.
- Caveat on the untouched bucket, load-bearing for anyone sizing from it: the matrix attributes no coverage to a subprocess, so gate.py main reads unreached without #13 even though two tests drive the CLI through a subprocess. The 15 is an upper bound on what needs a new test, and #13's in-process tests are the only ATTRIBUTED coverage of it.

STATE OF THE WORK: #13 stays a DRAFT at b7097a7. No cap change was made. The amendment question is with opum-doc as a combined A/B. This note changes no status and files no test.

RULING, DEC-195 (6), 2026-10-20T03:25:59Z, relayed by the leader: option A. test-skills#13 does NOT land and the cap is NOT amended; 0.929 kills per added test is under DEC-195 (4)'s bar.

#13 is CLOSED, with a comment carrying the measurement: mutant-set digest 222210827aa01053cd8fc32c56202671a4b1467dfb8f64cd844f5eb0aecd6bae, +13 kills for 14 added cases, and 9 of the 13 on ground existing tests already reach. Its branch test/TS-11-tmx-critical-floor is KEPT for reference and is not to be deleted.

The value of #13 folds into TS-24's parametrisation work, which measured 41 candidates among the unreached mutants. The four reaches nothing else attributes (gate.py main x3, write_baseline x1) may come back ONLY as a measured slot request sized with TS-24's result, never on their own.

The durable record: both matrices are in .tmx (ts13-crit-with-b7097a7.json, ts13-crit-without-b7097a7.json, and ts13-pkg-with-b7097a7.json for the whole package; .tmx is gitignored as always), and the numbers are in the note above. opum-doc's own words on the measurement: one basis, an identical digest, and the 15 untouched functions honestly given as an upper bound.

Nothing changes in this task's status: TS-11 stays To Do, its AC0 floor is still unmet at the measured score, and that gap is now TS-24's work plus this task's remaining slices, not #13's.
